page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-4 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, supporting 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core execution. The AMD EPYC 7B13 processor delivers strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng testing, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is mixed; while cached small-block read bandwidth is weak, uncached large-block read and write bandwidths maintain average tier performance at 43.63 GB/sec and 30.48 GB/sec respectively. Passmark memory testing ranks in the bottom 10%, indicating potential bottlenecks for memory-intensive operations.

Given the low memory-to-vCPU ratio and weak multi-threaded decompression and compilation benchmarks, this instance is not suited for memory-heavy databases or massive parallel build pipelines. Instead, its strong single-core performance makes it highly cost-efficient for lightweight, compute-bound tasks that do not require large memory footprints. Appropriate workloads include single-threaded processing, basic web serving, and lightweight text processing.
